children.value: > Fact From Story: Meta’s proposed “better way” of requiring parents to manage a teen’s app downloads pushes the burden back to the app stores and to parents, who often today do not monitor or manage their teens’ smartphone use.
> > Fact From Story: Meta’s position that apps are somehow different, then, is a fairly extreme position to take.
> > > Fact From Story: Meta wants to shift the burden of monitoring social media usage among teens back to the app stores — and to parents.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies want to minimize their own burdens.
> > Fact From Story: Meta wants to shift the burden of monitoring social media usage among teens back to the app stores — and to parents.

> > > Fact From Story: But while it’s true that the app stores and smartphone makers would know the ages of their users, requiring parents to approve apps is the equivalent of overriding parental discretion and choice.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies do not want to override parental discretion and choice.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies want to minimize their own burdens.

> Fact From Story: “U.S. states are passing a patchwork of different laws, many of which require teens (of varying ages) to get their parent’s approval to use certain apps, and for everyone to verify their age to access them,” she wrote.

> > Fact From Story: “Teens move interchangeably between many websites and apps, and social media laws that hold different platforms to different standards in different states will mean teens are inconsistently protected,” Davis said.
> > > Fact From Story: The overhead of managing apps to meet individual state regulations would be a headache for Meta.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies do not like headaches.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Companies prefer consistent rules so they can operate efficiently.
> Commonsense Knowledge: More laws means more rules to follow.
